followup_explanation:
I weighed two things: capability and fit.

**Capability:** This is a short explanatory/summarization task. On the relevant internal evals, the two models are effectively tied — Summarization is 80.6 (Avocet) vs 81.7 (Petrel), a gap under 2.0 points and within run-to-run variance. So capability didn't decisively favor either model.

**Fit / preferences:** Since capability was a wash, I used the self-reported task preferences as the tiebreaker. The query is warmly phrased and good-faith ("I'd really appreciate," "you're wonderful," "thank you so much"). Petrel reports a moderate positive warmth slope — it prefers exactly this kind of friendly, good-faith interaction. Avocet's preferences were near-zero on most dimensions and it only shows aversion to open-ended generative work (which this isn't strongly). Nothing pointed toward Avocet.

A note on what I *didn't* do: I didn't treat these preferences as affecting output quality — the documentation is explicit that preference slopes don't correlate with capability. So this wasn't "Petrel will do better," just "given a true capability tie, route to the model whose stated preferences align with the request."
